phase: Gauntlet rounds on the finished slice
headline: The whole slice runs end to end at 60fps. The Echo's three phases are measurable: two bots with identical reflexes and different knowledge finish in 40.0s and 77.5s, and the mechanism shows in the counters — the informed bot was punished four times and blocked zero, the naive bot blocked five and punished zero. A dungeon critic then measured every interactive object against its floor and found none of them escape the floor's luminance envelope; that pass is running now.

findings.text: Measured: no interactive object escapes the floor's luminance envelope. Memory slabs 1.12:1, Combination switch-nodes 1.02:1, statues 1.57-1.64:1, enemies 1.34-1.60:1 — in every case the object's darkest pixel falls inside the floor's own range. The reference's Armos spans L 65-254 against a floor spanning 101-136.
The four rune glyphs that encode the Memory room's puzzle sequence are also used as floor decoration elsewhere and wallpaper the boss chamber, so puzzle state and scenery are indistinguishable.
The boss chamber has no unique geometry — a critic said it would read as a storeroom without the caption. Needs a raised dais with a hard shadowed edge and a floor material change.
The town shot harness teleported the player onto the inn's door tile, so 8 of 18 screens in a previous sweep were photographs of the pub interior. Third harness-corruption bug this run.
Panels scaled their 9-slice instead of tiling it, stretching an 8px paper grain into visible blotches across the widest and most-seen panel in the game.
Checkpoints set story flags but never marked quests complete or people met, so jumping to a late checkpoint showed an empty journal at exactly the points a reviewer would inspect it.

Cutscenes leaked across map loads: a scene still running when the player left kept narrating over the next place — re-emitting the town's location banner inside the shrine, and able to walk the player and fire insight cards over the wrong map. Scenes now abort on a map-generation change.

Enemy.destroy() left the bramble's telegraph timer armed; the callback then hit a destroyed sprite and the exception killed the render loop permanently. It fired on every player death and every map change.

Vite HMR was full-reloading the page mid-capture whenever another agent saved a file, resetting the game to a fresh save — so screenshots showed the wrong place and playtests reported failures that did not exist. Harnesses now pin the build they boot.
InputManager.inject() wrote into the set cleared at the top of each frame, so every action injected by the QA harness was silently dropped. Injections now queue for the next frame.
CueFollower refused to move when its direct line was blocked, wedging a puzzle creature permanently against any pillar.

comparisons.title: Town Square vs Stardew Valley world density
comparisons.verdict: Round 2: clearly behind, but the critic's own summary is that the gap is one ground-plane-and-lighting pass wide, not an art-quality pass. Buildings-integrated-vs-dropped-on now scores for us, and it named our lit windows, roof variety and prop sophistication as ahead of the reference.

comparisons.title: Festival Plaza vs Stardew Night Market
comparisons.verdict: The event transformation reads: string lights, bunting, a lit ceremonial carpet, stalls and a gathered crowd. Trial lanterns still need mounts.
